scope: Documentation-only: no app or browser behavior changes

tests.title: Future agent can recover a stale Tristr Flow Accessibility grant
tests.userStory: As a maintainer, I can distinguish an enabled-but-stale macOS grant from a shortcut-registration failure and recover without changing unrelated permissions.
tests.setupInstrumentation: Read the committed AGENTS.md and run the targeted documentation regression test.
steps: Confirm the note explains code-signature mismatch and the risk of installing ad-hoc builds.
Confirm recovery resets only ai.pazi.tristrflow, then relaunches and re-enables its entry.
Confirm verification calls for a physical shortcut test and an Allowed result in tccd logs.
expectedResults: The instruction is concise, actionable, and does not tell agents to broaden permissions or replace a working app with an ad-hoc build.
tests.notes: AGENTS.md diff reviewed; targeted regression test passed. Browser QA is not applicable because only repository instructions and their regression test changed.
